metawoRld project specification

Source: SPEC.md

Version: 1 (draft) · Status: under review · Applies from metawoRld 0.3.0

This document defines what a metawoRld project is on disk: its folders, identifiers, file formats and the rules every input channel must follow. It is the contract between metawoRld (which owns and validates the data) and the tools that put data in (DataFindR, the entry form, CSV imports, or any other program in any language).

The key words MUST, SHOULD and MAY are used as in RFC 2119.

1. Principles

  1. One door. Data become part of a project only by passing the intake gate (submit_study() or an equivalent check). Channels never write to data/.
  2. Plain, open files. Everything is text: YAML, CSV and JSON, readable without metawoRld. Data packages follow the Frictionless Data Package standard.
  3. Every value is traceable to a person or tool, a source document and a place in it, and every change is logged.
  4. Generic core, project-specific forms. What is extracted is defined by the project’s forms, not by metawoRld.
  5. Git is the history. The project is a Git repository; metawoRld adds meaning (provenance, verification) but does not replace Git.

2. Project layout

my-review/
├── _metawoRld.yml          project settings and criteria          (edited by people)
├── _rules.yml              vocabulary and value checks             (edited by people)
├── _analyses.yml           planned meta-analyses                   (edited by people)
├── people.yml              people and roles                        (§5)
├── searches.yml            search log                              (§6)
├── records.csv             one row per unique record               (§6)
├── screening.csv           screening decisions, append-only        (§6)
├── forms/
│   ├── extraction.yml      required: the extraction form           (§7)
│   ├── screening.yml       optional: title/abstract screening form
│   ├── <other>.yml         optional: e.g. rob2.yml, nos.yml
│   └── *.schema.json       generated JSON Schemas (do not edit)
├── prompts/                LLM prompts used by DataFindR (optional)
├── submissions/            staged, unverified data                 (§9)
│   └── <study_id>/<extraction_id>/ …
├── data/                   accepted data                           (§8)
│   └── <study_id>/ …
├── fulltext/               full texts (git-ignored; never published)
└── NEWS.md                 release notes                           (§12)

_metawoRld.yml MUST contain spec_version: 1. Website files (_quarto.yml, index.qmd, …) and generated folders (_site/, figures/) are not part of the data and are not covered here.

3. Identifiers

Thing Format Example
Study lowercase [a-z0-9-], 3–40 chars, usually first author + year (+ letter) hansen2019, hansen2019b
Report (DOI) DOI, lower-cased, no https://doi.org/ prefix 10.1000/abc.123
Report (PMID) digits 31772108
Record DOI if known, else pmid:<PMID>, else rec-<first 12 hex of SHA-1 of normalized title + year> pmid:31772108
Person lowercase [a-z0-9-], 2–20 chars, usually initials ahj
Extraction <UTC yyyymmddThhmmss>-<person or tool>-<form> 20261113T001502-ahj-extraction
Data point measurement_id, unique within a study, [A-Za-z0-9_.-] dp12
Search lowercase [a-z0-9-] pubmed-2026-11

A study is the unit of analysis (one cohort or trial). A report is one publication. A study has one or more reports; a report belongs to at most one study. Records (search hits) are reports before screening; an included record is linked to a study.

Study ids are chosen once and never reused.

4. Files common to all tables

  • CSV files MUST be UTF-8, comma-separated, with a header row, "" quoting as needed, and empty cells for missing values. Each CSV that holds data is described by a Frictionless Table Schema (generated from the forms).
  • YAML files MUST be UTF-8 YAML 1.1 that yaml::read_yaml() reads. Field names MUST NOT be words YAML reads as booleans (y, n, yes, no, on, off, true, false).
  • Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC: 2026-11-13T00:15:02Z.
  • Hashes are written sha256:<64 hex digits>.

5. People: people.yml 

people:
  - id: ahj
    name: Anders Hagen Jarmund
    orcid: 0000-0002-3923-1637      # optional
    roles: [admin, extractor, verifier, arbiter, screener]
tools:
  - id: datafindr
    name: DataFindR

Roles: admin (changes forms and settings), screener, extractor, verifier (checks values), arbiter (resolves disagreements). Every provenance, verification and screening row refers to a person or tool id from this file. E-mail addresses SHOULD NOT be stored.

6. Searches and records

searches.yml lists every search that was run (a re-run is a new entry):

searches:
  - id: pubmed-2026-11
    database: PubMed
    query: '"interleukin-6" AND preeclampsia'
    date: 2026-11-13
    results: 412
    person: ahj

records.csv has one row per unique record:

column required meaning
record_id yes §3
doi, pmid no identifiers
title, year, journal, authors title yes bibliographic data (authors ;-separated)
searches yes search ids that found it, ;-separated (or manual)
study_id no set when the record is linked to a study
duplicate_of no record_id this one duplicates

screening.csv is append-only; the latest row per (record, stage, person) is that person’s decision, and the latest consensus row per (record, stage) is the outcome:

column meaning
record_id §3
stage title_abstract or full_text
decision include, exclude or unsure
reason exclusion reason (free text or a criterion from _metawoRld.yml)
person person or tool id
kind individual or consensus
timestamp §4

PRISMA counts are computed from these three files only.

7. Forms

A form is a YAML file in forms/ using the node format introduced in metawoRld 0.1 (_type, _description, _required, _items, _values, _ref, _ref_allow), plus a header:

_form:
  name: extraction          # must match the file name
  kind: extraction          # extraction | assessment
  version: 1.0.0            # semantic version; major = breaking change
  entry:                    # how the entry form lays out tables (optional)
    rows: variable_name
    columns: group_id
    cells: [value1, value2, value3, sample_size]
    context: [method_id, timepoint, statistic_type, source, source_page]
  • forms/extraction.yml MUST exist and MUST define metadata (object) and data_points (array of objects).
  • An assessment form (screening, risk of bias) defines one object per study (or per record, for screening).
  • metawoRld::export_schemas() writes forms/<name>.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) and Frictionless Table Schemas. These are generated and MUST NOT be edited by hand.

8. Accepted study: data/<study_id>/ 

data/hansen2019/
├── datapackage.json      Frictionless descriptor (generated)
├── study.yml             identity and reports (system-defined)
├── metadata.yml          the extraction form's `metadata` part
├── data.csv              the extraction form's `data_points`
├── provenance.csv        where every value came from
├── verification.csv      reviewers' decisions per data point
└── assessments/          optional: <form>.yml per assessment form

study.yml:

study_id: hansen2019
reports:
  - doi: 10.1000/abc.123
    pmid: "31772108"
    role: primary           # primary | secondary
status: included            # included | excluded_after_extraction | retracted
form_version: 1.0.0         # extraction form version the data follow
notes: ""

provenance.csv has one row per data point (and one row with measurement_id = _metadata for the metadata):

column meaning
measurement_id data point, or _metadata
extraction_id the extraction (§9) the accepted value came from
agreed_with other extraction ids with the same value (;-separated)
person person or tool id that produced the value
channel entry_form, datafindr, csv_import, manual_edit, …
tool name@version, e.g. DataFindR@0.2.0
model LLM model, if any
source_sha256 hash of the full text the value was read from, if known
timestamp when the value was produced

verification.csv is as in metawoRld 0.2 (measurement_id, status, reviewer, timestamp, row_hash, note), with reviewer a person id.

datapackage.json lists metadata.yml, data.csv, provenance.csv and verification.csv as resources with a hash and, for CSV files, a Table Schema. It MUST include "metawoRld": {"spec_version": 1, "study_id": …, "form": "extraction", "form_version": …} and a licenses entry (default CC-BY-4.0).

9. Submissions: submissions/<study_id>/<extraction_id>/

A submission is one extraction of one study by one person or tool:

submissions/hansen2019/20261113T001502-ahj-extraction/
├── submission.yml        who, how, when, status, gate report
├── study.yml             proposed identity/reports (new studies only)
├── metadata.yml
├── data.csv
└── provenance.csv        optional: per-value details (e.g. LLM model)

submission.yml:

extraction_id: 20261113T001502-ahj-extraction
study_id: hansen2019
form: extraction
form_version: 1.0.0
person: ahj               # or a tool id
channel: entry_form
tool: metawoRld@0.3.0
source_sha256: sha256:…   # optional
created: 2026-11-13T00:15:02Z
status: pending           # pending | accepted | rejected | superseded
blind: false              # true: hidden from other extractors until reconciled
gate:                     # written by submit_study()
  checked: 2026-11-13T00:15:03Z
  errors: []              # schema / link errors (submission refused if any)
  warnings: []            # value checks from _rules.yml

Rules:

  1. A channel creates a submission with submit_study(), or writes the folder itself and then calls check_submission(). Submissions with errors are not written (or are marked rejected with the errors listed).
  2. Several submissions may exist for one study (dual extraction).
  3. accept_submission() (one extraction) or reconcile() (two or more) writes data/<study_id>/, records which extraction each accepted value came from in provenance.csv, and marks submissions accepted or superseded. Submissions are kept, so disagreements can be audited.
  4. When a study already has accepted data, accepting a new submission replaces the study’s data (with overwrite = TRUE); verification of data points whose id and values are unchanged is kept (row hashes, §10).

10. Integrity

  • Values: verification rows store a hash of the values they refer to (computed over the data point’s value fields with rlang::hash(), as in 0.2). A changed value invalidates its verification.
  • Sources: source_sha256 records which file a value was read from, without storing the file.
  • Files: datapackage.json holds a hash for every resource. check_project() recomputes them and fails if a data file changed without datapackage.json (and therefore provenance) being updated through metawoRld.
  • History: Git commits are the audit trail.
  • Releases: a release is a signed annotated Git tag (git tag -s, SSH or GPG key) archived on Zenodo with a DOI. A release MAY add an OpenTimestamps proof of datapackage.json hashes.

check_project() is the single check run locally and in CI. It exits with a non-zero status when it finds errors and reports, per study: schema and link errors, hash mismatches, data points without provenance, references to unknown people, and submissions left pending.

11. Channels

A channel is any program that produces submissions. It:

  • MUST produce files that pass check_submission();
  • MUST set person (or a tool id from people.yml), channel and tool;
  • SHOULD set source_sha256 and, per data point, source and source_page;
  • MUST NOT write to data/, records.csv or screening.csv except through metawoRld functions (add_records(), add_screening()).

Channels written in other languages validate against the generated JSON Schemas and the rules in this document; the authoritative check is check_submission().

12. Versions and releases

  • spec_version in _metawoRld.yml: this document’s version.
  • form_version in each form: bump major for breaking changes (renamed or removed fields), minor for added optional fields. Every submission and accepted study records the form version it follows, and check_project() warns when it differs in major version from the current form.
  • Dataset releases use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: major for a new form major version, minor when studies are added, patch for corrections. NEWS.md lists studies added or changed and pooled estimates that moved (a draft_news() helper is planned).
  • Data are released under CC BY 4.0 unless _metawoRld.yml says otherwise. Full texts are never released.

13. Open points

  • Whether assessments (risk of bias) of one study by several people are stored as submissions too (proposed: yes, same mechanism).
  • Whether screening.csv should also be written by DataFindR directly through add_screening() (proposed: yes; its cache then becomes optional).
